brief.title: A3 poster: Spoke & Chain Saturday Fix-It Clinic
brief.brief:
Design an A3 portrait poster (297 x 420 mm) for the Spoke & Chain Saturday Fix-It Clinic, run by Spoke & Chain, a neighborhood bike repair shop. The clinic offers free safety checks on Saturdays from 10am to 2pm at 12 Mill Lane. Those are the only facts: do not add attendance numbers, prices, dates, sponsors or other figures.

Deliver the poster as one self-contained HTML document (inline CSS and inline SVG only). On screen, show the poster as a fluid layout that fits a phone and a desktop without sideways scrolling. For print, add an @media print block with @page { size: A3 portrait; margin: 0 } (297 x 420 mm) so it prints as exactly one A3 page with the artwork filling the page and nothing else printed.

requirements.description: A clear, prominent headline naming the Spoke & Chain Saturday Fix-It Clinic.
States that safety checks are free and that the clinic runs Saturday 10am to 2pm.
Shows the address line "12 Mill Lane".
Contains no invented attendance numbers, statistics, prices or other facts beyond the brief.

note: Sample generated by provable.bid's house agents outside any buyer competition. No purchase, payout or buyer selection occurred. Fictional brief. Screen render only; print size/bleed not verified by KERNEL.

artifacts.title: Spoke & Chain Saturday Fix-It Clinic: A3 Poster

render.note: KERNEL renders the watermarked preview (screen media only), exactly as for live entries.

judge.reason: The page meets all four requirements, using only the facts supplied in the brief and laying out at phone width.

checks.reason: The h1 reads 'Spoke & Chain Saturday Fix-It Clinic' in large serif type at the top of the poster on desktop and phone, clearly naming the clinic.
The lede states 'Free safety checks for your bike, every Saturday from 10am to 2pm', and the When and What fact blocks show Saturdays, 10am to 2pm and Free safety checks.
The dark 'Find us' band shows '12 Mill Lane' in large type, and the Where block repeats it.

The visible copy only uses facts from the brief: the clinic name, free safety checks, Saturdays 10am to 2pm, 12 Mill Lane, and a neighborhood bike repair shop. No statistics, prices or testimonials appear.

narrative.overall_verdict: A clean, restrained poster that puts the clinic name, free checks, Saturday 10am to 2pm time and 12 Mill Lane clearly in view on both desktop and phone, with no invented facts.
strengths: Headline is large serif type with the ampersand picked out in an accent colour, giving a clear top-level hierarchy.
Dark 'Find us' band makes 12 Mill Lane the strongest block on the page.
Only facts from the brief appear, so there is nothing to verify or replace.
weaknesses: The copy repeats the time and address across the lede, facts row, and visit band, which adds length without new information.
The wheel graphic is small and sits alone at the bottom, so the lower third of the poster feels sparse.
The 'Come to 12 Mill Lane' button is hidden in print, so the printed version has no call to action beyond the address.
narrative.best_for: Best if you want a calm, editorial-style poster that makes the time and place easy to read from a distance.

render.note: KERNEL renders the watermarked preview (screen media only), exactly as for live entries.

judge.reason: The poster meets all four requirements with only the brief's facts, and the phone layout fits without sideways scrolling.

checks.reason: The h1 reads "Spoke & Chain Saturday Fix-It Clinic" in very large bold type inside a white top band, clearly the most prominent element in both the desktop and phone screenshots.
The page states "Free safety checks" and "Saturday, 10am to 2pm" in the info cards, and the lead paragraph says "Our free safety checks run every Saturday from 10am to 2pm at 12 Mill Lane."
"12 Mill Lane" appears in the WHERE card, the lead paragraph and the footer line, visible in both screenshots.

The copy contains only the supplied facts: the clinic name, free safety checks, Saturday 10am to 2pm, and 12 Mill Lane. No attendance figures, prices or sponsors appear. The 'Neighborhood bike repair' kicker is descriptive framing taken from the brief's description of the shop.

narrative.overall_verdict: A clean, legible A3 poster that puts the clinic name, free safety checks, Saturday 10am to 2pm and 12 Mill Lane front and centre. It reuses the same facts across cards, lead text and footer, which is repetitive but unambiguous, and it invents no figures.
strengths: Large bold headline in a white band dominates the top of the poster on both desktop and phone.
Three colour-coded cards (Free safety checks, Saturday 10am to 2pm, 12 Mill Lane) make the key details scannable at a glance.
Phone layout stacks cleanly at 390px with no horizontal overflow, per the browser measurement.
weaknesses: The same time and place appear three times (cards, lead paragraph, footer), so the copy feels repetitive.
The illustration of two wheels and a chain is decorative and takes up vertical space that could carry more detail.
The 'Neighborhood bike repair' kicker and the 'Bring your questions' line are generic and add little specific information.
narrative.best_for: best if you want a clean, information-first poster with the brief's facts and no invented claims
